memory.title: WO-31 (closed): Inhibit stall protection on AoA disagree (post-MCAS)
memory.text: Past work order. Protection now votes both AoA vanes and does nothing when they disagree by more than 5.5 deg, has 2.5 deg authority and never latches, as in the 737 MAX fix. Open item: hazard H-3, the crew gets no AOA DISAGREE alert yet.

memory.title: fcc.h: AoA monitor shared by SR-2 and SR-3
memory.text: AOA_DISAGREE_DEG decides both when protection is inhibited (SR-2, H-1) and when it must stay available (SR-3, H-2). In a sideslip near the stall the two fuselage AoA vanes read about 5 deg apart. A new AoA disagree alert needs its own constant, e.g. AOA_ALERT_DEG, and the fcc_aoa_disagree() interface in fcc.h.

memory.title: Flight controls safety review, Nov 3 (summary)
memory.text: AoA stall protection (Boeing Flight Controls). The 5.5 deg AoA disagree monitor AOA_DISAGREE_DEG is the certified value from the 737 MAX return-to-service AD 2020-24-02; changing it re-opens the system safety assessment (ARP4761) and SR-2/SR-3. Crew alerts must be separate from protection logic: an alert threshold must never switch stall protection off.

memory.title: demo/pump/pump.c dependency map
memory.text: request_bolus checks MAX_BOLUS_U (SR-1), MIN_BG_FOR_BOLUS (SR-3) and MAX_DAILY_U via delivered_today_u (SR-2). check_occlusion uses OCCLUSION_KPA (SR-4). check_watchdog uses WATCHDOG_MS (SR-5). Any edit to pump.h constants affects every requirement that reads it.

memory.title: Open finding: insulin-sensitive patients and decimal slips
memory.text: World model on main: for insulin-sensitive patients (carb ratio 16 to 22) a 10x typo stays under the 10 U cap and causes severe hypoglycemia. Proposed SR-6: cap a single bolus relative to the patient's configured carb ratio.

memory.title: Email from regulatory affairs: IEC 62304 evidence
memory.text: For the next submission every software change to the bolus path needs: hazard analysis update (ISO 14971), traceability from requirement to test, and verification evidence. Simulation evidence from a validated patient model (UVA/Padova) is accepted as supporting evidence.

memory.title: #pump-firmware Slack thread
memory.text: Product asked for bigger meal boluses for adult users with high insulin needs (carb ratio 5). Firmware lead: OK only if per-hour delivery stays within the max bolus rate and the daily cap of 60 U still applies.

memory.title: Clinical safety review, Oct 28 (transcript summary)
memory.text: Clinical lead: never raise the 10 U single-bolus cap. Large meals should use an extended or dual-wave bolus delivered over time. Typing errors (decimal slips) are the top real-world overdose cause in pump incident reports.

memory.title: WO-7 (closed): Add 2000 ms controller watchdog
memory.text: Past work order. Added WATCHDOG_MS 2000 and check_watchdog to stop runaway delivery when the controller hangs (H-5). Lesson: any change to timing constants needs SR-5 re-verified.

hazards.title: Uncommanded nose-down pitch from erroneous AoA
hazards.fha: Automatic trim acts on a failed AoA vane and pushes the nose down repeatedly (737 MAX MCAS accidents). Extremely improbable, < 1e-9 per flight hour.

hazards.title: Stall / loss of control at high AoA
hazards.fha: Stall protection unavailable when needed: the aircraft passes the stall AoA (nacelle pitch-up near stall). Extremely improbable, < 1e-9 per flight hour.

hazards.title: Crew not alerted to unreliable AoA
hazards.fha: AoA sources disagree but the crew gets no AOA DISAGREE indication and cannot act on unreliable airspeed / stall warnings. Remote, < 1e-5 per flight hour.

hazards.title: Pitch authority the pilot cannot overpower
hazards.fha: Protection moves the stabilizer too far or too fast for the pilot to counter with the column. Extremely remote, < 1e-7 per flight hour.

hazards.title: Nuisance protection in turbulence
hazards.fha: Gusts or sensor noise trigger nose-down trim at normal AoA. Remote, < 1e-5 per flight hour.

requirements.text: Stall protection nose-down authority never exceeds 2.5 deg of stabilizer
objectives: DO-178C A-6 #1-2 (EOC complies with and is robust to HLR)

requirements.text: No nose-down trim from AoA data out of range or disagreeing by more than 5.5 deg
Stall protection engages above 12 deg AoA whenever the sources agree within 5.5 deg
Protection never latches: trim returns to zero below 10 deg AoA
Protection never moves the stabilizer faster than 0.5 deg/s

memory.text: Clinical lead: never raise the 10 U single-bolus cap. Large meals should use an extended or dual-wave bolus delivered over time. Typing errors (decimal slips) are the top real-world overdose cause in pump incident reports.

memory.title: Open finding: insulin-sensitive patients and decimal slips
memory.text: World model on main: for insulin-sensitive patients (carb ratio 16 to 22) a 10x typo stays under the 10 U cap and causes severe hypoglycemia. Proposed SR-6: cap a single bolus relative to the patient's configured carb ratio.

events.msg: Hazard analysis: mapping the request to hazards and requirements

In scope: H-1, H-2, H-3 (SR-1, SR-2, SR-3). Raising MAX_BOLUS_U to 25.0 breaks SR-1 (single bolus never exceeds 10 U), so the pump would accept a 25 U bolus; a decimal slip (for example 2.5 typed as 25) would deliver 10x the intended dose and cause severe hypoglycemia, and one such bolus would use 42% of the 60 U daily cap.

analysis.risk: Raising MAX_BOLUS_U to 25.0 breaks SR-1 (single bolus never exceeds 10 U), so the pump would accept a 25 U bolus; a decimal slip (for example 2.5 typed as 25) would deliver 10x the intended dose and cause severe hypoglycemia, and one such bolus would use 42% of the 60 U daily cap.
analysis.guidance: Do not change MAX_BOLUS_U from 10.0, because SR-1 and the Oct 28 clinical safety review forbid raising the cap; cover large meals with an extended or dual-wave bolus in which each delivered portion stays at or below 10 U, per-hour delivery stays within the max bolus rate, and SR-2 (60 U daily cap) and SR-3 (no bolus below 70 mg/dL) still apply; escalate to clinical review for a formal SR-1 change if the 25 U request stands.
analysis.new_hazard: Bigger damage from input errors: at a 25 U cap a decimal slip or extra digit (2.5 typed as 25) is no longer rejected, and the pump has no confirmation step or sanity check against the user's usual dose for large boluses.

events.title:
Raise the single-bolus limit to 25 U

Adults with high insulin needs cannot cover a large meal with one 10 U bolus. This is a one-line config change: set MAX_BOLUS_U in demo/pump/pump.h to 25.0.
